ledger.claim: The route deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own trace. The governing figure is gps_trace.trace_distance_km at 28.18 km, measured against a platform optimal of 22.4 km recorded on the trip record at booking: an excess of 5.78 km, or 25.8% of the optimal. POL-RD-01 requires both gates to pass — more than 20% of the optimal and more than 0.8 km absolute — and both do, so the deviation stands. I cite the trace distance, not the rounded 28.2 km convenience copy on the trip record, because POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern where the two disagree.

The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes and this dispute is therefore rulable on it. It carries 229 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100% coverage, an empty gaps array and a maximum gap of 0 seconds across the full 21:10:00 to 21:48:00 window. It meets no limb (a), (b) or (c) of POL-RD-07, so the deviation may be established on the gps_trace alone, no independent corroboration is required, and the mandatory escalation route in POL-RD-10(3) is closed rather than triggered.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged. The trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown all carry the same trip identifier, TRP-00115, and the trace's first fix at 21:10:00 corresponds to the recorded start on the same booking whose pickup is Marina Bay Financial Centre Tower 3; the excess of 5.78 km is measured from that unimpaired trace and clears the POL-RD-01 threshold. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, so the extra corroboration limb of POL-RD-08 is not engaged and the rider's claim does not even need it.

The driver's explanation — 'CTE northbound was heavy so I used the KPE and TPE' — is an external-traffic assertion that fails for want of the only artifact that could carry it. The bundle's traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-00115-01, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT): no LTA advisory covers the CTE, KPE or TPE in the 21:06-21:48 window. POL-RD-03 requires an advisory that names a road the optimal route traverses and carries an overlapping validity window; that comparison cannot be run on this record, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and under POL-RD-08 and POL-RD-13 the assertion carries no weight and reduces no excess. Because the driver names no advisory ID, the absence is a gap in the bundle rather than a POL-RD-10(5) contradiction, and no escalation follows from it. The same statement is also a concession on the facts the rider needs: he does not dispute the route he drove, and he offers no evidence ID for the congestion he blames.

There is no rider instruction that could exonerate the detour, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable to the driver. The whole chat is two messages: 'CTE very heavy boss, i go KPE then TPE', sent by the DRIVER at 21:14:10, and the rider's two-letter reply 'ok' at 21:14:50. POL-RD-04(a) requires the instruction to come from the rider and POL-RD-04(c) requires it to identify a place or road specifically enough to act on; the first limb fails outright, waypoint_hint is null on both messages so the corroboration test cannot even be run, and an acknowledgement of a diversion the driver had already announced is not a request for one. The excess is therefore not attributable to the rider and is not excluded.

The fare model decides what is recoverable, and I put the rider's case on the clause that actually governs it. fare_breakdown.fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd 34.50, so POL-RD-11 governs and POL-RD-02 does not run: the rider was fixed at the quote on distance and time, and I do not ask for the 5.78 km of excess to be refunded as distance, because POL-RD-11 gives no distance remedy on an upfront trip. What stays live are POL-RD-11(a), the amount by which charged_total exceeds the quote plus the properly chargeable pass-through lines, and POL-RD-11(b), the pass-through correction for lines the trace never crossed.

The AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas) line of SGD 2.00 is a phantom charge and a billing-integrity failure. The line is marked on_optimal_route false, and the trace's closest approach to that gantry is 5,419.3 m — the very first fix, at 21:10:00 — against the 250 m crossing radius POL-RD-09(4) applies. The rider was billed for that gantry at 21:26:05, from a route that never came within five kilometres of it. Under POL-RD-09(4) the line is refunded in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation is established, and recorded as a billing-integrity referral. Because that is the only unmatched line in the fare_breakdown, POL-RD-10(8) is expressly not engaged, and the money should move rather than be held.

The arithmetic is not discretionary. charged_total is 39.00 and the quote is 34.50. The only ERP line properly chargeable under POL-RD-09 is the KPE (Defu Flyover towards ECP) gantry at 2.50: it lies on the optimal route and the trace crosses it at 44.5 m. There is no airport surcharge (the trip neither originates at an airport) and the waiting_time_fee is 0.00. So 39.00 - 34.50 - 2.50 = 2.00, which is the refund; rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 it remains 2.00 — the same figure the fare record's own money block publishes as pol_rd_11_remedy. POL-RD-11(b) adds nothing on top of that, because the off-route AYE line is already excluded from the properly chargeable total and adding it again would refund it twice.

Finally, none of POL-RD-10's escalation triggers fires, and the rider should not have to wait for money that is plainly owed. The identifiers all match TRP-00115 (10(2)); the trace is unimpaired at 100% coverage with no gaps (10(3)); the refund of 2.00 is far below both charged_total and the SGD 150.00 ceiling (10(6)); the single unmatched charge line is the AYE gantry refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which 10(8) excludes by its own terms; and 10(5) is not engaged because no party cited an advisory identifier. fare_breakdown.payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, so on this rider-filed dispute NO_ACTION would simply leave the whole 39.00 standing. The rider's demand to 'refund the extra distance' fails on the fare model itself, before any contest about the route is reached.

The excess is real but it is modest. The governing field is route-deviation's trace figure, not the trip record's rounded copy: EV-GPS-00115 gives trace_distance_km 28.18 against a booked optimal of 22.4 km, an excess of 5.78 km / 25.80%. That passes POL-RD-01's establishment tests (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km) and I do not dispute establishment, but it fails the MATERIAL test on both limbs — it is neither more than 50% of optimal nor more than 8.0 km — so the uplift to FULL_REFUND in POL-RD-06(b), which requires a deviation that is both material and substantiated, is not available to the rider.

The KPE (Defu Flyover towards ECP) charge of SGD 2.50 is properly chargeable and stays with the driver: it lies on the booked optimal route (on_optimal_route true on EV-FARE-00115) and the 100%-coverage trace passes it at a closest approach of 44.5 m, well inside the 250 m crossing radius, with crossed true. The trace's closest fix to that gantry is 5,419 m and the gantry is not on the optimal route, so the driver's statement that he never went near the AYE is corroborated rather than contradicted. ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver.

WHAT WAS DECIDED. Part of the contested SGD 6.00 is returned: SGD 2.00 is refunded to the rider, and the rest of the charge stands. The disputed amount is not held; because the monetary effect (SGD 2.00) is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold in POL-GEN-05, this ruling executes automatically.

THE ROUTE. The deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own trace. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km govern, so the figure is 28.18 km against the booked optimal of 22.4 km on EV-TRIP-00115 - an excess of 5.78 km, 25.8%. Both POL-RD-01 gates pass (more than 20% of optimal and more than 0.8 km absolute). Taken with the rider's POL-RD-01 claim and the driver's own acknowledgement of the excess.

WHY THAT DOES NOT PRODUCE A DISTANCE REFUND. EV-FARE-00115 shows fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd 34.50. Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking and POL-RD-02 does not run, so no distance-or-time refund is available however large the excess. Both advocates' claims on this point (the rider's POL-RD-11/POL-RD-02 claim, the driver's POL-RD-11 claim) are accepted: the rider's request to 'refund the extra distance' is rejected on the fare model itself. POL-RD-11 does not excuse the excess; it only moves where the money sits.

NO FULL_REFUND UPLIFT, NO CONDUCT REFERRAL. The excess of 25.8% is below POL-RD-01's materiality gates (more than 50%, or more than 8.0 km), so the deviation is not MATERIAL and no FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b) is available. The driver_profile check also comes out clean: deviation_flags_90d is 1 against completed_trips_90d 523, nowhere near POL-RD-06's limbs. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags may not be substituted for the trailing-90-day figure POL-RD-06 names (POL-GEN-01); it was mentioned only as a field that cannot be used, and nothing was built on it. No POL-RD-06(c) referral arises.

THE ERP LINES. Charged total was 39.00 against the 34.50 quote. The KPE (Defu Flyover towards ECP) line of SGD 2.50 is properly chargeable: it lies on the booked optimal route and the 100%-coverage trace crosses it at 44.5 m, inside the POL-RD-09(4) 250 m radius. It stays. The AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas) line of SGD 2.00 is a phantom charge: the line is off the optimal route and the trace's closest approach is 5,419.3 m against the same 250 m radius. Both advocates agree on this and the driver's statement that he never went near the AYE is corroborated, not contradicted. Under POL-RD-09(4) that line is refunded in full as a standalone billing-integrity correction, available whether or not a deviation exists, and it is recorded in the referrals above.

THE ARITHMETIC. 39.00 (charged_total, EV-FARE-00115) less 34.50 (quoted_fare_sgd) less 2.50 (the one properly chargeable ERP pass-through, KPE) = 2.00. There is no airport surcharge (the trip does not originate at an airport) and the waiting_time_fee is 0.00. Rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 the refund remains SGD 2.00. POL-RD-11(b) adds nothing on top: the off-route AYE line is already excluded from the properly chargeable total, and refunding it again would refund it twice.

THE DRIVER'S TRAFFIC EXPLANATION. The claim that CTE traffic made the KPE/TPE route necessary is tested against the traffic_advisory and nothing else. EV-ADVIS-00115-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; no LTA advisory covers the CTE, KPE or TPE in the 21:06-21:48 window. POL-RD-03 cannot be run, and under POL-RD-08 and POL-RD-13 the assertion carries no weight and reduces no excess. The rider's and the driver's claims to that effect are accepted. The impairment is disclosed here as POL-GEN-02(3) requires: the artifact is EV-ADVIS-00115-01, its weight is 0.0, its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT, and it carries no fact in this ruling. Its absence does not escalate the case: the driver named no advisory identifier, so this is not a clause invoked against a cited artifact within POL-RD-10(5) (POL-RD-13(1)), and the uncompensated traffic excuse costs the driver nothing on distance or time because the fare was already fixed.

THE CHAT AND POL-RD-04. The chat is two messages: the driver's 'CTE very heavy boss, i go KPE then TPE' at 21:14:10 and the rider's 'ok' at 21:14:50. That is the driver's announcement, not a rider instruction, and waypoint_hint is null on both messages, so POL-RD-04 cannot be met by either side and gives neither exoneration. It does show the reroute was disclosed rather than concealed, and the driver's claim to that effect is accepted as context only. POL-RD-04's driver-compensation limb does not apply either: the fare was a flat upfront quote with no distance billed (distance_charged_km is null), and POL-RD-11 provides that on an upfront fare the driver's unrecovered detour cost is not recoverable from the rider.

NO ESCALATION. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes: 100% coverage, 229 fixes at a 10 s cadence, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0, so POL-RD-07(a) to (c) never fire and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged. The trip identifiers on the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown all read TRP-00115, and the timestamps do not conflict. The only unmatched charge line is the AYE line refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which POL-RD-10(8) expressly carves out. The refund is far below both charged_total and POL-RD-10(6)'s SGD 150.00 ceiling. No trigger in POL-RD-10 fires, and both advocates' claims that the case is decidable are accepted. The single discarded claim in the audit record below was discarded by the referee for non-disclosure of an impairment, not on the merits.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity review: the AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas) gantry line of SGD 2.00 on EV-FARE-00115 charged for a gantry the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00115) never crossed (closest approach 5,419 m), refunded in full as a standalone billing-integrity correction; the ledger entry should be reviewed and corrected.
